title: Infra GPU Fleet, Networking & IaC Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended practices for GPU fleet capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC module layout, CI/CD for infra changes, and operational runbooks. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for GPU-backed inference services.

Scope
-----
- GPU fleet capacity and procurement guidance (cloud and bare-metal).
- Cloud account and networking conventions needed for private deployments and hosted regions.
- Terraform / IaC module structure, release cadence, and CI/CD pipelines.
- Runbooks for common operational tasks and incident response.

Principles
----------
1. Single source of truth: Terraform modules are canonical for all cloud infra changes.
2. Safety first: deploy changes behind a canary and automated safety gates.
3. Observability-driven capacity: capacity decisions guided by utilization, P99 latency, and queue depth.
4. Reproducibility: manifests and module versions must be pinned in release branches.

Ownership & Contacts
--------------------
- Infra Platform (owner): infra-platform@redwood.ai
- GPU Fleet Team (day-to-day): gpu-fleet@redwood.ai
- Networking (VPC & peering): cloud-networking@redwood.ai
- Oncall rotation: refer to eng-sre oncall schedule page

Key SLOs & Targets
------------------
- API P99 latency SLO pockets (for inference serving) should remain within tolerated bounds; infra must ensure <10% request throttling due to capacity.
- Fleet utilization target (steady-state): 60% -- 75% (by GPU memory across nodes).
- Emergency headroom: maintain 15% immediately available capacity for spike absorption.
- Scaling latency: horizontal scaling should add capacity within 5–10 minutes for cold starts; warm-pools should scale under 90s.

GPU Fleet: Types, Tagging, and Procurement
------------------------------------------
- Supported instance types: Nvidia H100 (preferred for highest throughput), Nvidia A100 (secondary), and lower-tier T4 for batching/embeddings workloads.
- Tagging conventions (cloud tags + terraform tags):
  - redwood:service = inference-runtime
  - redwood:env = prod|staging|dev
  - redwood:gpu_type = h100|a100|t4
  - redwood:pool = dedicated|shared|spot
  - redwood:owner = <team>@redwood.ai
- Procurement guidance: aim for a mix of reserved (Dedicated) and spot/ephemeral capacity for cost balance. Default buffer = 15% reserved + 10–20% spot for burst.

Capacity Planning Process (Quarterly)
------------------------------------
1. Data collection: aggregate GPU memory utilization, per-model token/sec, average sequence length, per-route TPS and queue depth for last 90 days.
2. Forecasting: run workload growth model (90-day and 12-month) and translate to required GPU-hour commits.
3. Safety margin and procurement recommendation: recommend reserved capacity based on 75% utilization target and include 15% emergency headroom.
4. Approval & purchasing: PR -> finance review -> cloud procurement -> tagging.

Networking & Cloud Accounts
--------------------------
- Account structure: separate cloud accounts for prod, staging, and dev; additional accounts per-enterprise-customer for Private deployments where required.
- VPC design:
  - Per-region VPCs with standardized subnetting (10.<region>.<az>.0/24 style), public/private subnets per AZ.
  - Private endpoints for internal services (S3, SecretsManager).
  - VPC peering and Transit Gateway usage for multi-account connectivity; use central networking account as hub.
- Security groups: minimal ingress rules; apply service-level security groups (e.g., inference-runtime-ssh, inference-runtime-nfs).
- Egress & NAT: use centralized NAT gateways in each AZ for stable egress IPs required by some customers.

Terraform / IaC Modules (recommended layout)
-------------------------------------------
- repo: infra-modules (monorepo of reusable modules)
  - modules/gpu-node (launch templates, drivers, nvidia-runtime config)
  - modules/gpu-cluster (asg / instance group abstractions, autoscaler hooks)
  - modules/vpc-standard (VPC, subnets, route tables, endpoints)
  - modules/network-hub (transit gateway, peering)
  - modules/iam-baseline (roles, instance profiles, least-privilege policies)
  - modules/bootstrap (cloud-init templates, driver installers, monitoring agents)

Recommended module variables (example table)
- module: modules/gpu-node
  - instance_type: (string) e.g. p4d.24xlarge / h100-equivalents
  - gpu_count: (number) GPUs per instance
  - ami_id: (string) base AMI with CUDA drivers
  - bootstrap_script_url: (string) S3 URL to cloud-init
  - tags: (map) tags to apply

Module development & release process
-----------------------------------
1. Feature branch and unit tests: every module change must include Terraform unit tests/plan checks with terratest or tfsec where applicable.
2. Pull request: require 2 approvers from infra-team and at least one security reviewer for IAM/network changes.
3. CI checks: terraform fmt, validate, plan (against a mocked environment), static security scans (tfsec), and license checks.
4. Release: tag semantic version (vX.Y.Z) and publish to internal registry (artifact storage).

CI/CD: Pipelines & Safety Gates
-------------------------------
- We use GitHub Actions for module CI and a dedicated pipeline in our CD system (Spinnaker/ArgoCD equivalent) for environment promotion.
- Pipeline stages for infra changes:
  1. Preflight (lint, fmt, tfsec, terratest)
  2. Plan (generate plan and upload as artifact)
  3. Approvals (manual if plan changes > threshold: 5% capacity or changes to security groups/iam)
  4. Apply (run in a dedicated runner with least-privilege credentials from CI vault)
  5. Post-apply validation (smoke tests, monitoring alerts suppression check)

Canary & Rollout Strategy for Fleet Changes
-------------------------------------------
- For changes that affect launch templates, instance configs, or autoscaler behavior:
  1. Create a canary ASG with 5–10% of instances in a single AZ.
  2. Run smoke tests for model inference throughput & P95 latency for 30 minutes.
  3. If metrics pass, promote to additional AZs in increments of 25% until 100%.
  4. If regressions are detected, rollback via terraform to previous module tag and run postmortem.

Operational Runbooks (high-level procedures)
--------------------------------------------
- Node OOM / GPU memory pressure:
  1. Detect via monitoring alert (gpu.mem.free < 8% P95 across cluster).
  2. Isolate by cordoning node and draining pods (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets).
  3. Reprovision node with larger instance type or move pods to warm-pool nodes.
  4. If recurring, add to capacity increase request and schedule kernel/driver investigation.

- GPU Driver Upgrade (maintenance window)
  1. Prepare AMI with updated drivers in staging.
  2. Run canary upgrade in single AZ (5% of fleet).
  3. Validate telemetry and per-model quality checks.
  4. Roll forward across AZs with 1-hour windows between waves.

- Scale Up (manual emergency)
  1. Verify demand signals (burst queue depth, 95th-percentile token latency).
  2. If spot capacity insufficient, request cloud account team to spin on-demand instances using a predefined terraform param file.
  3. Notify customer-facing teams and update status page if user-visible impact expected.

Monitoring & Alerting Requirements
----------------------------------
- Metrics to collect per node: gpu.utilization, gpu.mem.free, gpu.temperature, node_cpu, node_memory, pod_queue_depth.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - gpu.mem.free P95 < 10% for 5m -> SEV2
  - host GPU temp > 85C for 1m -> SEV3 (auto isolate)
  - cluster-wide utilization > 85% for 10m -> SEV1 (scale/evict decisions)

Templates & Example CLI snippets
-------------------------------
- Terraform plan for a region (example):
  export TF_VAR_region=us-west-2
  terraform -chdir=envs/prod apply -var-file=prod.us-west-2.tfvars -auto-approve=false

- Promote module release:
  git checkout -b release/module-name-v1.2.0
  bump-version.sh modules/gpu-node v1.2.0
  git push && create PR -> CI runs -> merge -> tag -> publish-artifact

------------------------

Appendix: Quick checklist for a non-breaking infra change
-------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Create feature branch and update module with pinned version
- [ ] Run all CI checks (fmt, tfsec, terratest)
- [ ] Include smoke tests for inference perf in PR
- [ ] Plan shows no >5% capacity removal or security changes without manual approval
- [ ] Prepare rollback plan and tag previous module version

End of playbook. For questions or to request exception for a specific customer, contact infra-platform@redwood.ai
